Affordable Hotels West Palm Beach

  • July 29, 2026
  • Karen Escalera

 

 

 

By Amber Love Bond and Yours Truly

 

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 7:11
Instaread

West Palm Beach makes an easy escape for beach days, buzzy restaurants, and a little Palm Beach glamour, but you don’t need a splurge-level hotel budget to enjoy it. There are actually plenty of hotels offering solid Tripadvisor ratings and rooms that can often be found for $250 per night or less, depending on the dates. If you go at this time of year you might catch some summer sales as well. Here are our picks for affordable hotels West Palm Beach,

 

From downtown hotels close to the action to intimate, character-filled hideaways, these affordable hotels West Palm Beach make a polished South Florida weekend feel much more attainable. Spend an afternoon browsing the boutiques and galleries along Clematis Street or at CityPlace, then book dinner at spots like Hullabaloo, Avocado Grill, or E.R. Bradley’s before heading toward the waterfront for a sunset stroll. With the Norton Museum of Art, the Kravis Center, and the beaches of Palm Beach all within easy reach, there is plenty to fill a long weekend without ever straying too far from your hotel. Stay tuned until the end for links to posts on the best restaurants in Palm Beach, best shops and things to do.

 

 

West Palm Beach Marriott

If you want a dependable hotel in a convenient location without spending a ton of money, West Palm Beach Marriott is an easy choice. It is close to the convention center, Kravis Center for the Performing Arts, and CityPlace, so you’re near shopping, restaurants, and plenty of places for a drink or dinner. There is also an outdoor pool, fitness center, and on-site dining, which makes it a nice option for a weekend when you want the comfort of having everything right there.

The rooms are classic and comfortable rather than overly trendy, but the location does a lot of the work. It is a good fit for a quick girls’ weekend, a concert or event downtown, or anyone who wants to spend the day exploring West Palm and cross the bridge in just a few minutes to Palm Beach for dinner without committing to Palm Beach hotel rates.

 

 

Residence Inn by Marriott West Palm Beach Downtown

Residence Inn by Marriott West Palm Beach Downtown is the kind of place that makes a weekend feel a little easier. The rooms are suite-style with kitchenettes, there is complimentary breakfast, and you have more space than you would at a typical downtown hotel. This hotel is especially nice if you are traveling with a friend or family, are staying for more than a night or simply like being able to keep snacks, wine, and coffee on hand.

This hotel is very close to CityPlace, Clematis Street, and the waterfront, so you can head out for dinner or shopping without getting back in the car every time. While it’s not the most stylish hotel, it’s genuinely convenient, comfortable and a smart value for travelers who would rather put more of their budget toward meals, shopping, and activities. Plus it’s just a seven minute drive over the bridge and to Worth Avenue where strolling and people-watching is an activity in its own right.

 

 

Hotel AKA West Palm

Hotel AKA West Palm is for the traveler who wants their hotel to feel a little more special. The design is polished and modern, with a calm, residential feel that makes it a great choice for a couples’ weekend, a staycation or a girls’ trip where everyone wants somewhere cute to get ready before dinner. In that same central location, it’s walking distance from CityPlace and all of downtown restaurants, plus it’s just a few blocks away from the Royal Park Bridge, meaning you can be on Palm Beach in minutes where you can check out iconic restaurants like Buccan or spend some time exploring the Flagler Museum.

This is not a huge resort with endless amenities, but there are 217 ultramodern studios, one- and two-bedroom suites with full kitchens, a rooftop pool, and two spots on-site for cocktails and bites: a.lounge and The Blind Monk restaurant.

 

More Affordable Hotels West Palm Beach

Hilton West Palm Beach

Located right beside the convention center, Hilton West Palm Beach puts you in the middle of the action, with restaurants, shopping, and nightlife all within walking distance — that is, if you decide to leave. This hotel has the kind of pool scene that can turn a regular hotel stay into a little vacation.The resort-style deck is a major draw, especially if you want to spend a few hours in the sun before getting dressed for dinner.

It’s a bigger, busier hotel than the boutique properties on this list, but it has a fun energy and plenty of amenities. This is a great choice for a girls’ weekend, a group trip or anyone who wants to be able to walk to dinner somewhere cool like the RH Rooftop next door, check out the exhibits down the street at the Norton Museum of Art, grab a cocktail at nearby Eataly and still come back to a hotel that feels lively and well equipped.

 

 

Casa Grandview

Casa Grandview is the one to book if you want your hotel to feel like part of the getaway. Set in a historic home in Grandview Heights, this small boutique inn has individually decorated rooms, tropical gardens and a pool, with a relaxed, romantic feel that is very different from a standard downtown hotel. It feels personal, peaceful, and a little bit like finding a hidden spot that you want to keep to yourself.

You are still close enough to reach downtown West Palm Beach, the waterfront and Palm Beach easily, but coming back here feels like a break from the busier parts of town. Casa Grandview is especially lovely for a couples’ weekend, a solo reset, or anyone who would rather stay somewhere with charm and personality than a big lobby and a corporate hotel bar.

 

Rounding out the list of affordable hotels West Palm Beach

Grandview Gardens

Grandview Gardens has a quiet, tucked-away feel that makes it a lovely option for travelers who don’t need a huge hotel experience. The small property is surrounded by tropical landscaping and has a pool, creating a peaceful little retreat in a historic neighborhood just south of downtown. It’s the kind of place where you can spend the day out shopping or at the beach (which is just a short five minute drive away) and come back to somewhere that feels calm and private.

The vibe is more Old Florida hideaway than glossy downtown hotel, which is exactly why it stands out. It is a great choice for a low-key couples’ trip, a solo weekend, or anyone who wants a charming place to stay while still being close enough to enjoy West Palm Beach restaurants, shops and the waterfront.
